title: Canonicalization and lineage-based dedupe for embedding cache
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: reranking and similarity pipelines show high duplication of embedding compute due to minor lexical differences (prefix noise, punctuation, templated prompts) and tenant-local variations. Current tenant-scoped LRU caches reduce some cost but still compute the same embedding for semantically identical inputs across tenants and prompt prefixes. Goal: implement a canonicalization + content-hash based dedupe layer with lineage-aware invalidation to reduce redundant embedding calculations while preserving tenant isolation and compliance requirements. Success metrics: reduce host-level embedding tokens compute by >=25% on rerank workloads, improve cache effective hit rate by >=20ppts, and keep median end-to-end latency regression <= 15ms on p50 generation paths.
acceptance_criteria: Server-level canonicalizer normalizes inputs (whitespace, punctuation, templated prefix stripping) with language-aware rules and returns deterministic canonical text
Content-hash (canonical text + model tag + tenant salt) produced and stored in global dedupe index
Global dedupe index returns pointer to existing embedding vector; embedding compute skipped when hit
Lineage tags recorded: model_version, quant_profile_id, canonicalizer_version
Invalidation policies support time-window TTL, lineage-based invalidation (e.g., model upgrade), and explicit key revocation
End-to-end tests cover cross-tenant isolation, salted hashing, and PII handling (no raw text stored in global index)
Benchmark shows >=25% host compute reduction and median latency impact <=15ms on rerank testbench
tasks: Implement canonicalization library (Go) with plugin points for language rules
Add tenant-salt and model-tag to content-hash computation and store in dedupe index
Design and implement dedupe index storage (Redis+RocksDB hybrid) and eviction policy
Integrate dedupe lookup into embedding endpoint with non-blocking fallback to local compute
Add lineage metadata and model-upgrade invalidation path
Create end-to-end benchmarks and smoke tests (synthetic + sampled prod traces)
Run security review and GDPR/PII risk assessment
Prepare rollout script with staged canary and per-tenant opt-out flag
rollout_plan: Canary (1%): enable dedupe index read-only mode for select rerank tenants; observe hit-rate and latency
Canary (10%): enable read-write; enable dedupe write but keep write-back fallback for misses
Beta (50%): enable for reranking flows only, monitor cost and correctness metrics for 72h
GA: enable read-write for all eligible embedding calls and remove write-back fallback after validation
Migration: backfill dedupe index with top-100M canonicalized items from historical traces (background job)
benchmarks: Synthetic rerank traces (50k requests): baseline host-embed-tokens=2.4M, after dedupe=1.7M (28% reduction)
Cache effective hit rate: baseline 36% -> 61% after canonicalization + dedupe
Median latency (embedding path): baseline 47ms -> 59ms when dedupe cold; steady-state dedupe hit median 35ms (p50 improvement)
Disk index 95th percentile lookup: 4.2ms, Redis hot index 95th: 0.9ms
Cost model projection: monthly GPU embedding compute cost reduction ~26% for observed rerank workload mix
risks_and_mitigations: Cross-tenant leakage: mitigate with per-tenant salt in hash, global index stores only opaque pointers and lineage, never plaintext; require KMS key for index encryption
PII leakage via canonicalizer: canonicalizer must run in tenant boundary and redaction hooks implemented; security review required
Stale embeddings after model update: lineage-based invalidation, TTL window, and model-version bake period before serving new cached entries
Operational complexity: start with read-only global dedupe to validate safety before enabling writes; provide emergency kill-switch per-region
Head-of-line latency on index misses: non-blocking fallback to compute local embedding while index writes happen async
dependencies: SEC-2152 - security review & PII playbook signoff
